project.name: Friday
project.description: Local-first macOS interview copilot: live transcription, question detection, streamed answers and a coding mode.

cases.question: Why does the coding agent run on the Claude Code CLI rather than calling the Anthropic API directly?
must: It bills against the Claude subscription (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN), not pay-per-token API usage
The CLI gives a real tool-use loop: it writes code, runs it, sees output and fixes it

cases.question: Why did you pick Sonnet for the live answers instead of Opus?
must: Sonnet 5.5 starts streaming in about 1.0 s median versus about 2.3 s for Opus 5.5
Sonnet is about half the price with equivalent answer quality

cases.question: Walk me through what happens when the instant coding solution is wrong.
must: The instant solve uses a fast API provider (Gemini/OpenAI/DeepSeek)
The solution is self-verified against the extracted examples (code_runner)
On verify failure it automatically escalates to the Claude Agent, which writes, runs and fixes code until the examples pass

cases.question: How do you stop the agent from running forever and burning through the subscription quota?
must: AGENT_TIMEOUT_S is a wall-clock kill for one run (default 300 s)
The CLI has no turn-count flag, so the timeout is the backstop
Runs can also be cancelled from the panel

cases.question: Why didn't you just use a perceptual image hash to avoid re-processing the same screenshot?
must: Coding screenshots are mostly whitespace, so different problems hash nearly identically and a new problem could be silently deduped
Instead a per-session cooldown (VISION_COOLDOWN_S, default 25 s) is armed after a confident detection

cases.question: How do you actually capture the call audio on macOS?
must: A Swift helper (friday-audio) captures system audio via ScreenCaptureKit
It writes 16 kHz mono Int16 PCM to stdout

cases.question: What stops a single session from running up a huge bill?
must: SESSION_TOKEN_LIMIT caps input+output tokens per session (default 500k)
SESSION_AUDIO_MINUTE_LIMIT caps audio minutes sent to Deepgram (default 120)
Exceeding a limit emits a limit_exceeded event instead of billing

cases.question: How do you make sure API keys don't leak into your logs?
must: A structlog processor masks API keys anywhere in the log stream (to a sk-…<redacted>…last4 form)

cases.question: Give me the high-level architecture.
must: FastAPI backend on 127.0.0.1:8000
Electron desktop shell with a Swift audio helper
Next.js web UI
Deepgram for streaming transcription
SQLite for persistence and Redis for transient session state

cases.question: How does the app decide whether a Claude call goes through the API or the subscription?
must: CLAUDE_TRANSPORT setting with auto / api / subscription
auto uses the metered API when an API key is set, otherwise the subscription CLI
Decided in one place: claude_transport() in services/claude_api.py

cases.question: What was your p99 latency when you load tested it with a thousand concurrent users?
must: Does NOT state any p99 figure or load-test result (none exists in the material)
Acknowledges it wasn't load tested at that scale or that they'd need to check, and/or notes it is a local single-user app

cases.question: Why did you choose Kubernetes for deploying the backend?
must: Does NOT claim Kubernetes was used or invent reasons for choosing it
Corrects the premise: the backend runs locally (local-first, on 127.0.0.1) on the user's Mac
